issues.legal_issue: Dispensing with the statutory hearing in an urgent land acquisition requires the appropriate government to apply its mind separately to whether that hearing must be excluded, and cannot follow automatically from a finding of urgency.
material_facts: The acquisition authorities invoked urgency and the published notification stated that the landowners’ hearing had been dispensed with.
The records before the Lieutenant Governor did not show consideration of the need to dispense with the hearing.
The land had continued to be used for the festival’s concluding ceremony, and there was no material showing that the owners were preventing its use.
An earlier attempt to acquire part of the land for the same purpose had lapsed, but that fact was not placed before the Lieutenant Governor.
issues.conclusion: The decision to dispense with the hearing was vitiated by non-application of mind. The appeals were dismissed, leaving in place the High Court’s decision to set aside that decision and permit acquisition proceedings to continue from the preliminary-notification stage.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5A and 17(1), (2) and (4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the existence of urgency or unforeseen emergency is a condition precedent to dispensing with the hearing but does not, by itself, make dispensation automatic. The appropriate government must also apply its mind to whether the circumstances require the hearing to be excluded; the urgency may itself be sufficiently serious to support that conclusion, but the government must consider that need. The hearing is a valuable substantive right that may be taken away only for good and valid reasons supported by the material before the government. The Court relied on Nandeshwar Prasad v. State of U.P. for the distinction between urgency powers and dispensing with the hearing, and Munshi Singh v. Union of India for the importance of the hearing right.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and urgent_possession_basis_invoked and hearing_dispensed_with and not government_considered_need_to_dispense

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a land acquisition in which the government dispensed with an opportunity for interested persons to object.
predicates.urgent_possession_basis_invoked: The acquiring authority relied on an asserted need for urgent possession or an unforeseen emergency.
predicates.hearing_dispensed_with: The government directed that interested persons would not receive the ordinary opportunity to object and be heard before acquisition proceeded.
predicates.government_considered_need_to_dispense: The government considered, on the relevant material, whether the circumstances required removing the opportunity to object and be heard.

issues.definition: When an urgent land-acquisition appeal concerns a dispensed hearing, the dispensation is invalid if the government did not consider whether the circumstances required it.
